text:
South Carolina Chapter Robert F. Fartin 205 East Hillcrest Drive Greenville, South Carolina
Pecember 29, 1975
Rederal Power Commission Jashington, D.C. 20125
Subject: Draft Environmental Statement
Bad Greek Project Duke Power Company
Oconee County, South Carolina
Gentlemen:
As president of the South Carolina chapter of Trout Unlimited, I would like to inform you that, due to new information concerning the negative impacts of the promosed Bad Greek Pumped Storage Project, we plan to make formal comments by January 15 to the Draft Environmental Statement and license amplication. The documentation submitted in this draft includes data and conclusions which are no longer valid in light of these new developments.
Specifically, in Volume II, page w5-2 the statement is made that "indigenous fish inhabiting the streams and lakes of this area are not migratory, therefore, the design, construction and subsequent operation of the Bad Creek Pumbed Storage Facility need not be concerned with fish migration." This is fictually incorrect since a large spawning run of rainbow and brown trout has and is occurring in the lower reaches of Howard Greek below the proposed project. It is admitted that Howard Greek will be destroyed as a cold water habitat. (Volume I, Exhibit S, p. 5 "during construction and for a significant period of recovery, conditions in at least 3.5 miles and 9.2 acres of Howard Crees will be rendered unsuitable for trout habitation from Highway 171 Gownstream to Lake Jocessee"). The spawning run has been documented by the South Carolina Wildlife and Duke rower fishery biologists in November and December, 1975. A survey of tributaries to Lake Jocassee by South Carolna Chapter Trout Unlimited personnel indicates that Howard Greek is the only tributary in South Carolina which receives a spawning run. This, coupled with the poor condition of the remaining waters under Duke rower control due to their present timber harvest and land management practices, makes this new fishery resource extremely valuable.
The observed runs of trout and impact of the project on the stream fishery has been discussed in revised Sections 2.2.2.2, 3.1.2.3, 3.2.2.3, and 9.2 of The Bad Creek Final Environmental Impact Statement.
